The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

Goldman Sachs brings $100 billion Treasury fund into crypto’s institutional plumbing. The bank is bringing its roughly $100 billion Treasury fund to institutional crypto firms without creating a tokenized version of it. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

The restaking gold rush is over, and top protocols are barely making a profit. As restaking yields dried up and smart-contract risks mounted, Ethereum's top liquid restaking protocol walked away from its core business to build a crypto neobank instead. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Tether is a ‘lifeline’ for Iranian regime, Senate Dems say in new report. Democrats on the Senate's Permanent Subcommittee on Intelligence published a report alleging that USDT had become a key tool for the Iranian government. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

AI agents could drain cheap bank deposits, Apollo's Torsten Slok warns. AI agents could trigger a bank run by automatically moving household cash from low-interest checking accounts to higher-yield alternatives, Slok warns. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Chainlink launches new version of its crypto bridge tech 'CCIP' to give apps more control over their security. The new software lets companies add custom security checks so they do not fall victim to the same type of vulnerabilities that plagued rival bridges. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

THORChain rejects Bitget request to block hacker as $6 million moves to bitcoin. CoinDesk found 27 successful swaps moving about 2,390 ETH into 75.2 BTC, even as Bitget urged THORChain to stop serving addresses tied to the $387.5 million theft. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $83,540 with a -1.44% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $2,683.57 with a -0.39% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

The Stablecoin Statement specifically addresses stablecoins that are designed to maintain a stable value relative to the US dollar (USD) on a one-for-one basis, [...] On December 16, 2025, the FDIC issued a notice of proposed rulemaking (the Proposal) to implement Section 5 of the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for US Stablecoins Act (GENIUS Act). The GENIUS Act, enacted by Congress in July 2025, created a federal regulatory framework for stablecoins whereby a subsidiary of an insured depository institution could be approved to issue payment stablecoins.

items.title: Cryptocurrency Regulation: A Guide to U.S. & Global Policies | Britannica Money
items.description:
Cryptocurrency regulation in the United States has historically been fragmented, with federal agencies applying different interpretations based on the nature and use of each asset. That splintered approach began to change in 2025, when Congress passed legislation to establish a clearer framework for stablecoins and digital asset markets.

## Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs [...] Cryptocurrency regulation is no longer a theoretical debate—it’s an evolving framework that is beginning to take shape worldwide. In the United States, Congress made progress in 2025 toward establishing federal oversight of stablecoins and digital asset markets. One measure—the GENIUS Act—was signed into law. [...] In the U.S., landmark legislation enacted in July 2025 has begun defining the roles of federal agencies in regulating stablecoins and digital commodities. Although implementation is ongoing, these laws represent a shift away from case-by-case enforcement and toward a structured national policy.

## How cryptocurrency is regulated in the U.S.

items.title: U.S. Crypto Market Structure Reform: Is This the Bill That Will Redefine Bitcoin, ETFs, and Crypto Exchanges in 2026? - Bitcoin Foundation
items.description:
Here’s why 2026 could reshape U.S. crypto rules: institutions are already deep in. Not just dabbling – full entry via spot Bitcoin ETFs, Ethereum offerings, stablecoins, even digital versions of real-world assets. These pieces link directly to legacy financial systems. What still lacks is clear market structure laws. That gap defines the next phase.

### From Enforcement-Based Regulation to Formal Legal Framework [...] Banks could gain ground should regulations allow them to launch stablecoins, hold digital assets, and handle token-based settlements. Their edge? Years of meeting legal standards plus trust from big clients – something new crypto players lack, even though those startups adapt quicker. Speed favors the newcomers; maturity leans toward banks.

### Competition Between Stablecoins and Traditional Banking Systems [...] When rules are easier to understand, more people might choose ETFs because it feels safer for those making investment choices. Confidence in the actual trading market helps market participants do their job better, too.

## Stablecoins and Banking Integration

What holds money steady is now part of how systems move value. Because stablecoins handle transfers, clear trades, and back digital shares, they shape how Washington handles crypto rules.

The bullish case would strengthen if: [...] The White House's renewed support for clearer crypto regulation has strengthened expectations surrounding the future U.S. digital-asset framework.
